questions.q: What is Microsoft's current, official position on database mirroring, per this lesson?
options: It's deprecated, with Availability Groups recommended as the modern replacement
It's the current recommended default for all new HA deployments
It has been completely removed from SQL Server with no trace
It's recommended only for brand-new greenfield systems
questions.explain: Microsoft has marked database mirroring deprecated for a considerable time, explicitly recommending Availability Groups instead.

questions.q: Why does this lesson cover database mirroring at all, given its deprecated status?
options: A meaningful number of production systems built years ago are still running it, unmigrated, and it's worth recognizing
Because it's actually a secretly superior technology to Availability Groups
Because the course recommends deploying it on new systems
Because Microsoft is planning to un-deprecate it soon
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: this is about recognizing mirroring on inherited legacy systems, not recommending it for new work.

questions.q: What role does the 'mirror' play in database mirroring's principal/mirror/witness structure?
options: It continuously receives and applies log records from the principal, kept in a restoring state and not directly queryable
It actively serves the database to client applications
It's an optional component that only exists to enable automatic failover
It's a backup file stored on a network share
questions.explain: The mirror receives and applies transaction log records, staying in a restoring, non-queryable state, distinct from the principal.

questions.q: What does the optional 'witness' instance provide in a database mirroring setup?
options: The ability for automatic failover between principal and mirror; without it, failover must be manual
A read-only copy of the database for reporting
The physical storage the principal and mirror both write to
A required component without which mirroring cannot function at all
questions.explain: The witness is optional and specifically enables automatic failover; mirroring can run without one, but then failover is manual.

questions.q: You inherit a legacy system running database mirroring with no witness configured. What does that mean?
options: Failover between principal and mirror has to be initiated manually, since there's no third instance to enable automatic failover
The system will automatically fail over the instant the principal has any issue
The setup is not actually valid and mirroring cannot be running
A witness is not something that has ever been optional in mirroring
questions.explain: Without a witness, automatic failover isn't available — an administrator has to initiate failover manually.
